title: Azure Storage services and storage account types
learningObjective: Compare Blob, Files, Queue, Table and Disk storage, and describe storage account types and their options.
foundation: A storage account is a container for your Azure Storage data with a globally unique name (it becomes part of the URL).

Blob Storage: huge amounts of unstructured data (images, video, backups, logs). Azure Files: file shares you can mount over SMB or NFS. Queue Storage: messages between parts of an app. Table Storage: simple NoSQL key/attribute data. Disk Storage: block disks attached to VMs.
Different account types trade cost for performance: Standard (HDD-backed, most uses) or Premium (SSD-backed, low latency).
engineer: Blob: block blobs (text and binary, up to about 190 TiB), append blobs (logs), page blobs (random access, VHDs). Access over HTTP/HTTPS, REST, SDKs, AzCopy. Uses: serving images or documents to browsers, streaming video, backup and archive, data for analysis.
Azure Files: fully managed SMB and NFS shares; mount concurrently from cloud or on-premises; replace or supplement file servers; cache on Windows Server with Azure File Sync.
Queue Storage: millions of messages, each up to 64 KB, accessed over HTTP/HTTPS; used to create a backlog of work processed asynchronously.

Table Storage: NoSQL structured data with a schemaless design (Azure Cosmos DB for Table is the premium option). Disk Storage: managed disks (Standard HDD, Standard SSD, Premium SSD, Premium SSD v2, Ultra Disk).

Account types: Standard general-purpose v2 (blobs including Data Lake Storage, queues, tables, files; LRS, GRS, RA-GRS, ZRS, GZRS, RA-GZRS); Premium block blobs (LRS, ZRS); Premium file shares (LRS, ZRS); Premium page blobs (LRS, ZRS).
Endpoints: https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net, .file., .queue., .table., .dfs. (Data Lake). Names: 3–24 lowercase letters and numbers, unique across Azure.

animation.caption: Pick the storage service, tier or redundancy, then the right account type.

example.title: A photo-sharing app
body: Uploaded photos go to Blob Storage; an upload message goes to Queue Storage; a worker reads the queue to create thumbnails.
Photo metadata is stored in Table Storage, the worker VM's OS runs on a Premium SSD managed disk, and the design team shares assets on Azure Files.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription (a free account works)
permissions: Reader to explore; Contributor to create resources
portal: Create a resource > Storage account: performance (Standard/Premium), account kind, redundancy.
Storage account > Containers / File shares / Queues / Tables.
configuration.cli:
az storage account create -g <rg> -n st$RANDOM -l westeurope --sku Standard_LRS --kind StorageV2
az storage container create --account-name <account> -n photos --auth-mode login

expected: Blob for objects, Files for shares, Queue for messages
Premium accounts support only LRS or ZRS
failureScenarios: Expecting geo-redundancy on a premium account
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.cause: Names must be 3–24 lowercase letters and numbers and globally unique.

troubleshooting.symptom: Can't select GRS on a premium account.
troubleshooting.cause: Premium accounts support LRS and ZRS only.
troubleshooting.fix: Use Standard general-purpose v2 for geo-redundancy.

comparisons.difference: Blob is object storage over HTTP; Files is a mountable file share over SMB/NFS.
Queue Storage is simple and cheap; Service Bus adds ordering, topics and transactions.

misconceptions.myth: Managed disks are stored in your storage account.
misconceptions.reality: Managed disks are separate resources managed by Azure.

misconceptions.myth: Each storage service needs its own account.
misconceptions.reality: A general-purpose v2 account holds all four.

architectureDecisions: Use Standard GPv2 unless you need premium performance.
Use Blob for anything served over HTTP.
Use Azure Files to lift-and-shift file shares.
